You can merge the last two commits in Git by using the "git rebase" command with the "-i" option, which stands for "interactive". Here are the steps:

1. Make sure you're currently on the branch where the commits are. If not, use `git checkout your_branch_name`.

2. Start an interactive rebase with `git rebase -i HEAD~2`. `HEAD~2` here means that you want to include the last 2 commits in the rebase. If you want to include the last 3, 4, 5, etc. commits, replace the number `2` with `3`, `4`, `5`, etc.

3. After running the previous command, git presents an editor with a list of the last 2 commits, each represented by lines starting with the word `pick`. It should look something like this:

   ```
   pick 3fd90ab commit 1 message
   pick e5f4b49 commit 2 message
   ```

4. You need to tell git that you want to merge the second commit into the first one. To do this, replace the word `pick` on the second line with `squash` or `s` for short. This is how it should look like:

   ```
   pick 3fd90ab commit 1 message
   squash e5f4b49 commit 2 message
   ```

5. Save and close the editor. After this, git combines the two commits into one and opens another editor for you to change the commit message. The new commit message will automatically be a combination of the two old commit messages, but you can change this to anything you like.

6. After you've saved your new commit message and exited the editor, the rebase is complete. Your last two commits have been successfully combined into one. If you want to check the result, you can use the command `git log -n 2` to display the last two commits. You should now only see one commit instead of the original two.

Note: This process rewrites history. If these commits have already been pushed, you will need to use the `--force` option when pushing the changes. This is generally frowned upon if others have already based work on the commits you are modifying. Use with caution!
